The Bank of Korea (BOK) is considering buying gold for its reserves in the medium to long term, which would be its first gold purchase in more than a decade.

Heung-Soon Jung, director of BOK’s Reserve Investment Division, stated any purchases would depend on gold’s market trajectory, the evolution of Korea’s international reserves, and the performance of the Korean won.

The last gold purchase by BOK was between 2011–2013, after which it faced criticism due to a subsequent multiyear gold price slump. 

Global central bank gold purchases have recently surged, pushing gold prices to record highs (over $4,380/oz last week), fueled by currency debasement concerns and speculation on US interest rate cuts.
Despite the recent rally and correction in gold prices, central banks’ sustained demand has kept gold up more than 50% this year. Some central banks, like the Philippines, are considering selling gold to rebalance reserves as its share in their portfolios has grown significantly.

The BOK stores its bullion in London for liquidity, a practice followed by other central banks such as Mexico and Madagascar, while China is attempting to attract foreign gold reserves to be stored domestically for greater market influence.

Decisions on timing and scale of purchases will depend on ongoing monitoring of global markets by the BOK.​

https://t.co/VYLivavcnG

LOOK: Photos of the Manila Film Center in Pasay City taken on Tuesday, October 28.

Built in 1981 for the first Manila International Film Festival under former First Lady Imelda Marcos, the building became known for a tragic construction accident that trapped several workers. It is now regarded as one of the most haunted places in Metro Manila.

📷: John Louie Abrina | MB
